A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from Function Aligned Regression (FAR) to Gradient Aligned Regression (GAR). All 24 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v3, including proofs, experimental appendices, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, real-world benchmark results, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses and measured running times.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, network-depth experiments and PySR evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same MAE, error-variance and normalized pairwise-difference losses, KL-based aggregation and optimization procedure. FAR-to-GAR renaming and the explicit clarification that normalization constants are detached from backpropagation do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Concrete Compressive Strength replaces Abalone in the benchmark coverage. The two synthetic datasets and the other five real-world datasets remain, including both Parkinson targets and both AgeDB settings. PySR and network-depth experiments reuse the existing synthetic data.

E2.justification: v3 adds PySR as a supplementary synthetic comparator, evaluated with and without trigonometric functions in its search space (Appendix B.5). The original synthetic neural comparators and the eight real-world baseline methods retain their participation in corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include all seven nonempty loss-component combinations across six tabular tasks, a five-setting network-depth sweep with GAR alpha tuned over {0.5, 1, 2}, and controlled PySR search spaces. The original synthetic and retained benchmark protocols, including splits, budgets and tuning grids, are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 examines alpha sensitivity and efficiency but does not isolate loss components or vary network depth. v3 adds comprehensive component ablations (Table 4), depth sensitivity (Figure 6), and a symbolic-regression prior-knowledge analysis (Figures 4–5). Alpha sensitivity results also replace Abalone with Concrete Compressive Strength and revise Wine Quality.

E5.justification: Appendix B.8 newly specifies five AgeDB repetitions with different random seeds; v1 already reports means and standard deviations without this run-count disclosure. This does not establish an increase in runs. Existing synthetic five-seed reporting and benchmark Student's t-test practice remain.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Concrete results, removes Abalone and revises Wine Quality scores: FAR/GAR MAE changes from 0.596 to 0.494 and Pearson correlation from 0.503 to 0.613, without a disclosed protocol change. Parkinson through AgeDB entries remain identical. Table 2 replaces timings and expands coverage; new PySR, depth and ablation results include GAR's best overall ablation rank of 2.375 in Table 4.

T1.justification: The derivative-equivalence statement now explicitly limits derivative orders to 1 through K, and Appendix A.3 adds directional-limit and L'Hôpital reasoning. v3 omits v1's general p-norm error-difference corollary and MAE/absolute-error variance derivation. The principal variance, Pearson-correlation and KL-aggregation results remain.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient pairwise losses, gradient alignment and competitive regression performance remain. v3 explicitly narrows the abstract's scope to clean data without noise, outliers or distribution shifts and adds the claim that the two pairwise components are beneficial separately.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section explains that GAR can be misled when training data do not reflect the underlying function. v3 also explains why symbolic-regression comparisons depend on access to suitable function primitives. Benchmark correlations are interpreted primarily as evidence about rank preservation, replacing v1's stronger derivative/shape interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents AgeDB's 12,208/2,140/2,140 split, age range and 224-by-224 crop size, identifies IC50 categorical feature types, and clarifies gradient detachment. The printed code pointer changes from FAR to GAR. Most training details are retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cranmer and Petersen on symbolic regression, Klivans on outlier-robust regression, and Yeh for Concrete, while removing the Abalone reference. It makes the label-space versus latent-feature-space positioning more explicit; the central comparison with RankSim, RNC and ConR remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution narrative and substantial method discussion are rewritten. A new Motivations subsection precedes the pairwise-loss development, the derivative theorem moves later, a Limitations section is added, and experimental settings are reorganized into expanded appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v3 adds two PySR figures, a 25-panel network-depth figure and the component-ablation table. The runtime table expands from three to five dataset columns. Sensitivity displays are revised and reordered, and the duplicate main-text Wine Quality panel is removed. The original synthetic plots largely retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v1 does not isolate the contributions of its three losses and demonstrates synthetic behavior at only one network depth. v3's six-task component study and depth controls address these important validation gaps, while explicit clean-data limitations improve claim calibration. These are substantial evidential gains, although unexplained Wine Quality revisions remain a documentation weakness and Table 4 supports the best aggregate rank rather than superiority on every metric.
